subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our 45-min discovery so we’re aligned on pain, goals, and immediate next steps. See attached workbook (acme_tco_workbook.xlsx) and a short pricing summary (redwood_pricing_breakdown.pdf).

Pain / goals we heard:
- High per-token spend on current hosted provider; monthly bill growing with ML features rollout.
- Need predictable unit economics for search/chat endpoints used by product and support (peak traffic around 2pm PT).
- Regulatory requirement: data residency in us-west, audit logs for access.

Key numbers you shared:
- Current estimated monthly token volume: ~10M tokens (production) + 20M tokens projected in 3 months with feature ramp.
- Budget envelope for inference (this FY): $20k/month (hard constraint from finance).

Redwood TCO levers we discussed (summary):
1) Model selection & quantization — switching to a 4-bit quantized variant can reduce per-token cost ~20% with small quality delta.
2) Batching & dynamic routing — recommended batching policy for your 99th percentile latency target (250ms) reduces effective per-token cost by ~15% for bulk background jobs.
3) KV/prefix caching — caching repeated context for customer support chat can cut token consumption on repeated prompts by 30-50% depending on reuse.
4) Smart fallback / rollouts — use cheaper model variant for low-risk routes (e.g., system prompts) to reduce unit cost without degrading UX.

Preliminary 1-month TCO (baseline assumptions in workbook):
- Baseline (current provider): ~$28k/month (10M tokens, no batching/caching)
- Redwood estimate (with batching + caching + quantization): ~$14k–$17k/month (10M effective tokens after caching), representing ~40-50% saving.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the TCO workbook (attached) with line-item assumptions so you can run scenarios. (done)
2) Pilot: 30-day pilot on a subset of traffic (search index + support bot) to validate latency and realized token savings. We propose a pilot commit of $5k credit + standard pilot SLA.
3) Tech sync: Rafael (cc'd) will coordinate a 60-min PoC kick-off to pin config (batch targets, cache TTLs, model variant).
4) Procurement: if pilot validates, aim for PO by Apr 15 to hit April production start.

Open questions for you:
- Can you confirm the 10M/month baseline (production only) number?
- Any hard latency SLOs besides the 250ms 99th?
- Who should Rafael coordinate with for the technical PoC (SRE contact)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if you want to walk through the workbook together.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: acme_tco_workbook.xlsx (XLSX, ~85KB)
Attachment: redwood_pricing_breakdown.pdf (PDF, ~45KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid recap and great to see explicit levers called out. A few quick clarifications:

- The 10M token baseline is for production only (correct). Our internal projection includes the +20M from feature ramp, but for procurement we need incremental spend delta.
- Latency SLO: 99th at 250ms for product-facing chat; search can tolerate up to 350ms.
- SRE contact: Priya (cc) is the right person for the PoC. She’ll also own perf validation.

On budget: finance gave us a hard constraint of $20k/month. The ranges you shared look promising — if Redwood can demonstrate the mid-point of the estimate (~$15k/month) in pilot, we have room to move forward.

Next: Priya — can you confirm availability for a PoC kick-off early next week? Procurement will likely want the workbook and a one-pager on billing terms.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
CTO, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Appreciate the quick reply Alex. Priya — great to have you looped in. Rafael and I updated the workbook with a pilot scenario and a conservative/vs. optimistic column; summary below. Full assumptions are in the attached workbook and the pricing breakdown.

Pilot scenario (30 days) — conservative assumptions:
- Traffic: route 25% of support bot + 10% of search traffic -> ~3.5M tokens/mo equivalent for pilot window.
- Expected realized savings during pilot with conservative settings: 30% (batching + caching + mild quantization) -> effective spend estimate for pilot: $2.8k (net of $5k Redwood pilot credit we discussed).
- Quality guardrails: A/B test on 10k sessions; rollback if any regression >2% NPS delta.

Full production (if pilot validated) — 10M tokens baseline:
- Redwood estimated spend (mixed model/quantization + cache): $14,200/month (mid-case).
- End-state unit economics assume 35-45% reduction vs current provider depending on traffic composition.

Procurement & billing notes (one-pager details):
- Standard monthly invoicing with net-30; enterprise contract available for Dedicated/private deployments.
- We can provide an initial invoice credit to cover pilot months; PO preferred if moving to prod after pilot.

Suggested next steps this week:
- Rafael: propose 3 time slots for PoC kick-off (60-min) — he’ll cover config and test plan.
- Priya: confirm one SRE + an analyst to validate token counts during pilot.
- Alex: if OK, I’ll loop in Procurement and send the workbook + one-pager.

Rafael — can you send calendar options?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
